messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] First preview release of RKWard 0.5.0 (KDE 4)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

as indicated in the recent announcement of 0.4.9pre1, I'd like to follow up 
0.4.9 with a release of the KDE 4 version of RKWard (0.5.0) quickly. I have 
now prepared a preview of this, available at 
http://rkward.sourceforge.net/temp/rkward-0.5.0pre1.tar.gz .

If you have a KDE 4 installation already, it would be nice if you could give 
this a test-run. With KDE 4's switch to using cmake as the new build-system, 
the installation process has changed for RKWard as well (and the 
source .tar.gz is 50% smaller). Instructions are available in the "INSTALL" 
file in the .tar.gz. The short version is:

Unpack the .tar.gz
Create a temporary directory somewhere, and cd there
Run "cmake /path/to/sources -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$KDEDIR"
Then the usual
# make
# sudo make install

Since the sources have changed quite radically while porting, all testing is 
very welcome.

---- Translators ----

.po and .pot files are provided in the .tar.gz as usual. Before working on 
your translations in detail, you may want to check whether everything seems 
ok with the .po files provided (the message extraction process changed as 
well). Final translations should be submitted by January 18 according to the 
current release plan, but you'll get another note before than.

 ---- Further timeline ----

Depending on the amount of feedback, there may or may not be a second preview 
release of 0.5.0, around January 14. If all goes well, the offical 0.5.0 will 
be released around January 21st.

Regards
Thomas

There is no obvious way to do this, but internally the console is a (heavily
misused) katepart, just as the script editor, so the same configuration applies
to both. So you can:

1. Open an editor window
2. Select Settings->Configure Editor->Fonts & Colors->Highlighting Text Styles
3. Select "Scripts/RKWard Output" from the dropdown (this is the highlighting
used in the console)
4. Adjust the properties of the "Output" style

Regards
Thomas

RKWard has performance issues when dealing with datasets containing many (tens
of thousands) items (or sub-items, such as elements in a list/environment).
GO is one of those packages, and I guess lumiHumanV1 is another. Frankly, I'm
rather surprised, you don't see the issue directly when loading lumiHumanV1?

Unfortunately this is a problem of the current design and not easily solved,
though at least some partial progress has been made. If you were using a version
of RKWard prior to 0.4.8, upgrading to 0.4.8 will improve the situation somewhat
(but probably not enough to be useful).

There is a bug-tracker at https://sourceforge.net/tracker/?group_id=50231&atid=459007
. You can also write about such problems to the rkward-devel mailing list (prior
subscription recommended, as this makes spam control easier for us):
https://lists.sourceforge.net/lists/listinfo/rkward-devel .

Regards
Thomas

By: tfry

Yes, after installing lumiHumanV1 I can see why it does not fail while loading.
This is because all the objects that cause the problem in lumiHumanV1GO are
inside another environment, which RKWard will not investigate by default. You
could - theoretically - avoid the hangup by making sure the large list never
exists in a place where RKWard would see it, e.g. by wrapping a "local({...})"
around the code in question. Of course this would only make sense, if the end
result of your computation is a more managable dataset, that you can then
assign/return to globalenv(). (Generally objects with many rows are fine (e.g.
data.frame's), only large lists / environments are a problem).

So, indeed, I guess for now the only viable solution is to use plain R for such
tasks. I'll keep the problem in mind, and I have some basic ideas on how to
fix this, but as mentionend, this is going to take some time.

Plant Disease Epidemiology and Ecology graduate level course at Kansas
State. The final product is a set of five documents that can be used for
classroom or self-taught learning of these concepts. For each specific
topic, students were asked to find three peer-reviewed articles
illustrating the topic as the basis for constructing each module.
Students worked with a post-doctoral research fellow and advanced
graduate student to construct each teaching module.

Our goal for these modules was to provide an open access publication
based on free software in order to expand the availability of teaching
materials for plant disease ecology and epidemiology to the widest
audience possible. All five modules have been reviewed and accepted by
Plant Health Instructor, http://www.apsnet.org/education/top.html.

The introductory document in particular mentions RKward.  Throughout the
rest of the documents the code is formatted in RKward syntax
highlighting by using the HTML export function.

Hi,

version 0.5.0 of RKWard is available for download, now. See 
http://rkward.sf.net for some more details. The new release is designed for 
KDE 4, and needs a least KDE 4 libraries to be installed.

Many thanks to all contributors, testers, translators!

---- Debian users: ----

Note: The debian package provided should be installable with
# dpkg -i --force depends rkward_0.5.0-1_i386_sid.deb
even if some dependencies have not entered the main archive, yet. However, a 
number of icons may be missing. 

---- Developers: ----

Feel free to commit changes of all sorts to SVN again. Please make sure to 
commit your changes to trunk (i.e. the KDE4 version). If you cannot use KDE4, 
yet, no problem: Just continue to use RKWard 0.4.9, but specify the 
pluginmaps from your SVN checkout under Settings->Configure RKWard->Plugins. 
This way you can work on the most recent versions of the plugins, without 
using the most recent version of RKWard.

Regards
Thomas
